title: Ambrose Digital - Activation Staging & Ops Sync
header:
Date: 2026-04-23 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Platform: Video call (recorded)
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Hannah (Redwood) + Sofia, Liam, Priya, Marcus, Evelyn (Ambrose)
summary: Kickoff for Ambrose Digital's activation staging environment. Reviewed networking and security requirements (VPC peering, KMS, SSO), validated the staging runbook and rollback plan, and agreed on metrics for pilot pass/fail. Action items assigned around test dataset provisioning, staging perf runs, and security docs review. Next step: Redwood to send staging checklist and SOC2/KMS artifacts; Ambrose to provision VPC and provide sample workloads for benchmark window next week.
action_items: Marcus Boyd - Provision staging VPC and create peering request (due 2026-04-27)
Diego Morales - Share staging runbook + perf test script + sample curl commands (due 2026-04-24)
Priya Singh - Verify KMS integration requirements and share key rotation policy (due 2026-04-29)
Sofia Patel - Provide 3 representative prompt sets and traffic profiles for pilot (due 2026-04-26)
Maya Chen - Send SOC2 summary, network diagram template, and costs estimate for dedicated vs hosted (due 2026-04-24)
next_steps: Redwood to provision staging cluster on reserved test capacity and share access window for benchmarks
Ambrose to complete VPC peering and hand over sample workloads
Schedule 90-min perf run and joint analysis the week of 2026-04-28
Security review follow-up to confirm KMS/HSM path and audit log retention
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Okay everyone, welcome. this is Maya from Redwood, Diego and Hannah are here too. thanks for carving out time. hey Sofia, how's the team?
00:06 Sofia Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. we're good, we just finished the last sprint so timing is great. Marcus and Liam are on to talk infra.
00:12 Marcus Boyd: yep, hey, quick background: we'll be using a staging VPC in eu-west-1, we want minimal egress and strict controls.
00:20 Diego Morales: perfect, that's what we expected. today we want to walk the staging activation checklist, network flow, and hammer out security bits so you can run an initial perf window next week.
00:30 Liam O'Connor: couple of things up front, latency SLOs for us are 120 ms p50, 280 ms p95 for chat flows, and cost is also a hard constraint — we're evaluating dedicated capacity vs hosted with caching.
00:45 Hannah Lee: makes sense. we'll map those SLOs to queueing and batching knobs in the runbook. Diego will show the perf script later.
00:51 Priya Singh: security is the other big one. we need SOC2 attestation summary, KMS integration or HSM option, and we require audit logs forwarded to our SIEM for 365 days.
01:00 Maya Chen: absolutely. we have a SOC2 summary and an audit log retention playbook, i'll send those today. for KMS you can choose customer-managed keys — Redwood supports KMS with envelope encryption — or we can run a dedicated HSM path for the private deployment.
01:14 Priya Singh: spelled out: how does key rotation work? and are logs hashed / tamper-evident?
01:20 Diego Morales: Rotation is compatible with usual KMS patterns; we rotate envelopes and don't re-encrypt old cache blobs, we maintain key versions. audit logs are signed and shipped to your S3, you can pump into the SIEM. i'll follow up with the exact schema. apologies if some of the terms get munged in transcription.
01:34 Evelyn Tran: for project planning — what do we need to have ready from our side to run the perf tests?
01:38 Diego Morales: sample workload: 3 prompt sets, synthetic traffic profile, and a small dataset for embeddings if you test retrieval. Marcus, that'll live in the staging bucket.
01:46 Marcus Boyd: yes we'll spin that up. i have a question on network: do you require VPC peering or can we use PrivateLink?
01:52 Maya Chen: we support both. PrivateLink often simplifies egress rules, but peering is fine if you prefer direct network access. there are small tradeoffs — PrivateLink can add a bit more latency but isolates routing.
02:05 Liam O'Connor: ok if we do peering we need a playbook for route tables and a sample security group.
02:10 Diego Morales: i'll upload a network diagram and sample Terraform snippets — they'll be in the runbook.
02:15 Priya Singh: about data residency: some logs will stay in eu-west-1, but can you guarantee any tokenization or PII redaction before storage?
02:23 Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted mode can be configured with data retention policies and optional auto-redaction for PII in logs. for Private deployments you have full control — logs never leave your VPC unless you opt in.
02:33 Sofia Patel: we will likely start hosted in staging and then move to dedicated if perf and cost look right. curious — what quantization and model variants do you recommend for lower cost without losing response quality?
02:45 Diego Morales: good question. for conversational flows we often suggest a 4-bit quantized smaller variant for higher throughput; but for hallucination-sensitive flows you may want to pin to a full-float or 8-bit-quant variant. Redwood Optimize can profile your prompt sets and recommend quantization profiles; we'll share a prior recommendations deck.
03:00 Marcus Boyd: speaking of profiling, how do you handle KV cache when a model is rolled forward? we have sessions that rely on long contexts.
03:07 Diego Morales: KV cache is preserved within a model version. cross-version compatibility is limited so we recommend session handoff guidelines in the runbook — small warmup requests or prefix caching to reduce cold-starts.
03:20 Hannah Lee: i'll note that in the runbook section called "session persistence and rollouts".
03:26 Evelyn Tran: can we get a staging access window with credentials for our SREs?
03:30 Maya Chen: yes, we'll provision temporary keys and a read-only monitoring view. Diego — what's the usual window for perf runs?
03:36 Diego Morales: we typically do a 2-4 hour stress window with ramp-up and steady-state for 1 hour. that lets us measure p50/p95 and token cost. it matches the 52 minute call we're in, ha.
03:46 Marcus Boyd: fine. we'll target next Thursday morning for the benchmark.
03:50 Maya Chen: great. next — rollbacks and failover. we support canary rollouts with auto-fallback to safe variants if latency or error rate spikes. we'll add thresholds to the runbook.
04:03 Priya Singh: what about compliance reviews? we need a formal security questionnaire and an NDA addendum for auditors.
04:09 Maya Chen: we'll attach the security questionnaire and a standard addendum. if you need extra controls we have an enterprise package with extended logging and HSM integrations.
04:18 Sofia Patel: on timelines, assume we're aiming to go-live beta in 6 weeks. what are typical blockers you've seen?
04:24 Hannah Lee: common blockers are network provisioning delays, missing sample workloads, and disagreements on SLOs. with the runbook and action items we usually clear those within 2-3 weeks.
04:34 Marcus Boyd: ok i'll chase the VPC peering this afternoon.
04:36 Evelyn Tran: any training or enablement materials for our internal teams?
04:39 Maya Chen: yes, we'll provide a runbook, an admin playbook, and a short recorded walkthrough. plus a one-hour enablement session after you pass staging.
04:49 Liam O'Connor: pricing question: how do you show cost difference between dedicated and hosted during pilot?
04:54 Maya Chen: we provide an estimated unit-cost breakdown — tokens, embeddings, reserved GPU amortization. Diego can produce a modeled cost for your traffic profile once you submit the prompt sets.
05:05 Diego Morales: i'll run the costing model after Sofia sends the prompts.
05:08 Sofia Patel: i'll send them by tomorrow.
05:11 Maya Chen: perfect. let's recap action items quickly — Marcus to provision VPC, Diego to send runbook and perf scripts, Priya to validate KMS, Sofia to send prompt sets, Maya will send SOC2 and network diagram. then we schedule the perf window.
05:29 Priya Singh: small nit: in our policy we require log integrity proofs for audit. is that supported?
05:34 Diego Morales: yes — we can provide signed log digests and chain them to S3 object versions.
05:40 Maya Chen: ok thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts in a single thread and schedule the perf run.
05:46 Evelyn Tran: thanks everyone, good meeting.
05:48 Maya Chen: thanks — talk soon.
